ro.name: Palazzo del Capitano del Popolo

ro.name: Pozzo della Cava

ro.name: Fortezza Albornoz

ro.name: Chiesa di Sant'Andrea
ro.text: Biserică veche cu un turn dodecagonal rar, construită pe locul unui templu roman și al unui centru creștin timpuriu.

en.name: Duomo di Orvieto
en.text: A masterpiece of Italian Gothic architecture, famous for its mosaic-covered facade and Signorelli's frescoes.

en.name: Pozzo di San Patrizio
en.text: A 16th-century well, 53 meters deep, featuring a double-helix spiral staircase designed for donkeys to haul water.

en.name: Orvieto Underground
en.text: A complex network of over 1,200 man-made tunnels and caves carved into the tufa rock since Etruscan times.

en.name: Torre del Moro
en.text: Standing 47 meters tall in the city center, this clock tower offers an unparalleled 360-degree view of Orvieto.

en.name: Palazzo del Capitano del Popolo
en.text: An elegant 13th-century palace built from local tuff rock, formerly the home of the People's Captain.

en.name: Pozzo della Cava
en.text: An Etruscan-origin well and cave system in the medieval quarter, featuring pottery remains and ancient cisterns.

en.name: Museo Claudio Faina
en.text: Located opposite the Duomo, this museum houses one of Italy's finest private collections of Etruscan artifacts.

en.name: Fortezza Albornoz
en.text: A 14th-century fortress built by Cardinal Albornoz, now a city park with dramatic views over the valley.

en.name: Necropoli del Crocifisso
en.text: An Etruscan burial ground at the base of the city's cliffs, with over 200 tombs dating from the 6th century BC.

en.name: Chiesa di Sant'Andrea
en.text: A historic church on Piazza della Repubblica featuring a unique 12-sided tower and archaeological crypts.

en.name: Piscina Comunale
en.text: The municipal public swimming pool serving the community of Orvieto.

descriptionAdvanced.de: Orvieto scheint direkt aus dem vulkanischen Gestein gewachsen zu sein, auf dem es steht. Die Stadt in Umbrien bietet eine einzigartige Kombination aus etruskischer Geschichte, mittelalterlicher Architektur und Renaissance-Kunst. Das unbestrittene Highlight ist der Duomo di Orvieto, dessen Fassade mit schimmernden Mosaiken und filigranen Skulpturen zu den schönsten Italiens zählt. Im Inneren beeindruckt die Cappella di San Brizio mit Fresken von Luca Signorelli, die Michelangelo beeinflussten. Doch Orvieto bietet auch unter der Erdoberfläche Sensationen: Ein riesiges System aus Tunneln, Brunnen und Kellern zeugt von der jahrtausendelangen Nutzung des weichen Gesteins. Der Pozzo di San Patrizio, ein architektonisches Meisterwerk mit zwei ineinander verschlungenen Wendeltreppen, wurde gebaut, um die Stadt im Belagerungsfall mit Wasser zu versorgen. Heute ist Orvieto eine 'Cittaslow', die für Lebensqualität und traditionelles Handwerk steht.
descriptionAdvanced.hu: Orvieto mintha közvetlenül abból a vulkáni kőzetből nőtt volna ki, amelyen áll. Az umbriai város az etruszk történelem, a középkori építészet és a reneszánsz művészet egyedülálló ötvözete. A vitathatatlan csúcspont az Orvietói Dóm, melynek csillogó mozaikokkal és finom szobrokkal díszített homlokzata Olaszország egyik legszebbje. Odabent a San Brizio-kápolna Luca Signorelli freskóival nyűgözi le a látogatót, melyek állítólag Michelangelóra is hatással voltak. De Orvieto a föld alatt is tartogat szenzációkat: alagutak, kutak és pincék hatalmas rendszere tanúskodik a puha kőzet évezredes használatáról. A Szent Patrik-kút, ez a két egymásba fonódó csigalépcsővel ellátott építészeti remekmű, azért épült, hogy ostrom idején is vízzel lássa el a várost. Ma Orvieto a 'Cittaslow' mozgalom tagja, a magas életminőség és a hagyományos kézművesség városa.
descriptionAdvanced.ro: Orvieto pare să fi răsărit direct din stânca vulcanică pe care este cocoțat. Orașul umbrian oferă o combinație unică de istorie etruscă, arhitectură medievală și artă renascentistă. Piesa centrală este fără îndoială Domul, a cărui fațadă decorată cu mozaicuri strălucitoare și sculpturi migăloase este considerată una dintre cele mai frumoase din Italia. În interior, Capela San Brizio adăpostește frescele lui Luca Signorelli, care au servit drept inspirație pentru Michelangelo. Orvieto ascunde însă și o lume subterană fascinantă: un sistem vast de tuneluri și peșteri săpate în tuf. Puțul Sfântului Patriciu (Pozzo di San Patrizio), o capodoperă inginerească cu scări elicoidale duble, a fost conceput pentru a asigura alimentarea cu apă în caz de asediu. Astăzi, orașul este un simbol al mișcării 'Cittaslow', promovând un stil de viață tihnit și meșteșugurile tradiționale.
descriptionAdvanced.en: Orvieto appears to have grown organically from the volcanic tuff rock it sits upon. This Umbrian city is a stunning tapestry of Etruscan history, medieval architecture, and Renaissance art. Its undisputed crown jewel is the Orvieto Cathedral, featuring a facade of shimmering mosaics and intricate sculptures widely regarded as one of Italy's finest. Inside, the San Brizio Chapel showcases frescoes by Luca Signorelli that are said to have influenced Michelangelo. Beneath the city's streets lies another world: a vast network of tunnels, wells, and cellars carved into the soft stone over millennia. St. Patrick's Well, an engineering marvel with a double-helix staircase, was commissioned by the Pope to ensure water supply during sieges. Today, Orvieto is a proud member of the 'Cittaslow' movement, emphasizing quality of life, local traditions, and exquisite craftsmanship.
